verdicts.note: The 2026-10-08 single-vote rule is met: besides the ESSB 6346 Nay votes [S13], the dossier has independent Tier 1 Nay votes on ESSB 5813 [S15] and ESSB 5814 [S17], the Anacortes forum statement opposing 'taking money out of our pockets' to close the deficit [S12] (verified in the cached article), and a platform plank on fighting a property-taxing-authority increase [S4]. -2/high stands.

Two separate explicit statements to reassess and reduce county spending and sort expenditures into essential, valuable and nice-to-have [S9][S12] (verified in the cached articles). Counter-evidence considered: he wants behavioral health facilities fully funded [S12] and touts state capital dollars brought to east Skagit [S1][S10]; these are carve-outs and state-level appropriations, not a county investment stance, so -2/high holds.
Removing regulatory steps, faster permits and lower taxes on multi-family housing [S10][S12]; no public-housing or tenant-protection positions. -1/medium is appropriately modest.
Stands with law enforcement (FOP award) and supports Flock cameras [S4][S12]; co-responder sponsorship and the platform's 'root causes' line [S4] justify -1 rather than -2.

Council, mayor, senator since 2018 and Minority Whip [S1]; pamphlet says 'No other candidate has my depth of experience' [S1] and he called himself 'the most capable and experienced' at the July forum [S10] (verified).

Would preserve senior center and Meals on Wheels funding even where not required and warns against 'extreme cuts' [S11] (verified); campaign frames priorities as investment in roads, broadband and infrastructure [S3]. Budget-prioritization and transparency statements [S8][S9] keep it at +1/medium, not +2.

His direct answer on housing costs is permit streamlining, zoning for more housing types and infrastructure [S8] (verified), with a homeownership focus [S3]; no tenant-protection or social-housing positions. Workforce/middle-income work with cities and pushing back on state apartment mandates [S3] cut both ways, so -1/medium rather than -2.

Behavioral health, substance-use prevention, overdose response [S3] and North Star [S6] support the prevention pole. His Flock opposition is framed as distrust of the vendor's 'backdoor' [S11], not as a policing philosophy, so it adds little; +1/medium still holds on the behavioral-health evidence.

Although the appointed incumbent, he said he doesn't have decades of experience but brings 'new ideas, creativity and a willingness to learn' [S11] (verified in the cached article); nine months in office plus four council years [S6]. +1/medium is reasonable against Wagoner's -2.
